# One page header

What sits at the top of every page: the title at the left edge, one line under it, at most one filled button; a focused task’s name and its one exit; and the shell’s utilities kept out.

## The rule

Every page is one of three kinds (`pageKind`): a **list** (Goals, Check-in, Reviews, People, Metrics, Activity, Data, Help, Workspace), a **detail page** (a goal, a person, a team, a metric, a review, a past import, a Help article) or a **focused task** (any form: a check-in, the table check-in, New goal, Change a goal, set-up, a review's set-up, a metric's forms, the import, the wrap-up).

```
List or detail page                                      Focused task
‹ Goals                     (detail pages only)          Week 46 check-in · 2 of 7          ✕ Close
◯ Off track · 36 hours      (detail pages with a status)
Lead time for changes                [ Primary ] [ Watch ] [ More ]    What's the number this week?
Rhea Kapoor, CI/CD · Team goal · G-14 · Updated 14 Nov
```

1. **The title is at the content's left edge** on every width. Nothing sits to its left: a person's picture goes above their name.
2. **The app's utilities are the shell's** (`SHELL_UTILITIES`): Find, Demo and your avatar live in the sidebar on a computer and in the top bar on a phone, on every page, a goal's included. Never in a page's header.
3. **A long title gets a full-width line on a phone.** Below 700 px the header stacks: what sits above, the title, the line under it, then the actions in one row. On a list with a list bar (Metrics, People, Teams, Feedback), the one action goes to the end of the list bar instead, so the first row stays near the top. On a computer the actions sit at the right of the title's first line, and the title wraps before it pushes them.
4. **One filled button per header** (`headerButtons`): a list keeps one; a detail page one filled and one plain standing button ("Check in again" or "Watch"), then More; a focused task none, because its primary is the footer's ([one form footer](form-footer.md)). Earlier buttons win; the rest belong in More.
5. **List tools are not header actions:** Export, Views and Manage watching stay in the list bar, with the list they act on.
6. **A count is said once:** in the list's count line or a section's heading, in the header's line only when the page is that count.
7. **Sticky on scroll, on detail pages only:** one line of status, title, number, the primary and More (a goal's summary bar). On a phone, once that line is compact it takes the top bar's place: the top bar shows only at the very top of the page.
8. **The phone's top bar names the page only once the title has scrolled away** (`topBarSays`): until then it shows the workspace, Find and you, so the page's name isn't said twice on one screen. A page whose title is for screen readers only on a phone (Goals) is named at once. A focused task has no top bar.
9. **A focused task's header** has the task's name and where you are at the left (`taskLine`: "Week 46 check-in · 2 of 7"; one of one is the name alone) and its one exit at the right, worded by `closeWords`. When both don't fit (a phone, with "Discard draft" beside the exit), the exit keeps the right of the first line and the name goes under it. No back link: Back is the footer's.

The header is core, with no switch: every page uses it, so there is nothing to switch off.

**Built in Faro, and not yet (18 Nov).** Built: `PageHeader` on Home, Check-in, Reviews, People, a person, a team, Activity, Help and its articles, What's new, Settings, Workspace, Feedback, Data, Research, Start the next year, the wrap-up's list, Metrics, a metric, and the import's pages; `TaskHeader` on every focused task; Find, Demo and you out of a goal's header, in the phone's top bar on every page; the top bar's name once the title has gone; a list's action at the end of its list bar on a phone; a goal's compact line in the top bar's place. Not yet in Faro, so a rebuild should build them from the words above: Goals keeps its own header markup (its views, search and filters share the header's row and are tuned for the first screen, check P8), though it follows rules 1 to 3; a goal's page keeps its summary bar, which is the sticky line of rule 7 but isn't drawn by `PageHeader`; a review's agenda header, which F08 and UX1 are changing; the sticky line's height subtracted when scrolling to an anchor; and `headerButtons` choosing what goes into More on screen (each page passes the buttons rule 4 allows).

## Worked examples

Each is run against the real rule by `src/spec/spec.test.ts`: the result is what the code gives.

| Given | The rule gives |
|---|---|
| A goal’s page, Goals, and a goal’s check-in. | `detail, list, task` |
| The second of seven check-ins in week 46; then a single one. | `Week 46 check-in · 2 of 7 / Week 46 check-in` |
| A goal’s page offered Check in again (filled), Watch, Share and New goal (filled). | `Check in again, Watch \| More: Share, New goal` |
| People on a phone in the Platform workspace, its title in view, then scrolled away. | `Platform / People` |

## Where it lives

- [src/domain/pageHeader.ts](../../../src/domain/pageHeader.ts): `pageKind`, `taskLine`, `headerButtons`, `topBarSays`, `SHELL_UTILITIES`

## Requirements

- `PAGE-HEADER`: One page header, in three kinds. A list page (Goals, Check-in, Reviews, People, Metrics, Activity, Help) and a detail page (a goal, a person, a team, a metric) have the title at the content's left edge, with nothing to its left: above it a detail page's status line, under it one line (what's in scope; who and where), and at the right of its first line at most one filled button (a detail page adds one plain standing button, then More). Below 700px it stacks, and the title has a full-width line of its own. A focused task's header has the task's name and where you are at the left (“Week 46 check-in · 2 of 7”) and its one exit at the right; when both don't fit, the exit keeps the first line. Find, Demo and your avatar are the shell's, never a page's, and the phone's top bar names the page only once its title has scrolled away. The header is core: every page uses it, so it has no switch.
- `NAV-FORMS`: A form has one way out, top right, in words: “Close” until something is typed and then “Close and keep the draft” where a draft is kept (check-in, New goal, goal edit, set-up), “Close without saving” where nothing is (a review's set-up and edit, a goal's wrap-up), which first asks “Close without saving? What you typed here will be lost.” with Keep editing when something was typed.
- `NAV-BACK`: One back link per page, “‹ {where}” above the title, never on a place's first page: back to the last page in this tab that isn't a form and isn't this page, named as the menu names it, going back in the browser's history so Forward still works; the browser's Back onto a form you left steps over it the same way. Arriving from outside it goes to the page's parent: the goal a goal feeds, else Goals; the review for a goal in its walk; People, Teams, Help, Reviews.
